title: Announce the AudioView review toast to assistive tech
body:
## Summary
The review/fix toast in AudioView renders as a plain div with no role or live region, so screen-reader users never hear the outcome.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioView/index.tsx:115-129 renders `rvToast` as an absolutely positioned div with no `role="status"`/`aria-live`; the status dot is colour-only. The header Generate Audio System button (index.tsx:164) also lacks `type` and its icons are not aria-hidden. Fixed = `role="status" aria-live="polite"` on the toast (role="alert" for error), aria-hidden icons, type="button".

## Flow
- user runs Review from the Overview tab -> useModuleReviewCli calls onToast -> toast div appears -> the screen reader announces nothing
- fix: role/aria-live on the toast container, type + aria-hidden icons on the header button

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users learn whether review/fix succeeded; measured by a render test finding getByRole("status"). Nothing visual changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - review outcome is announced
Before: 0 live regions on the toast (read index.tsx:115-129)
After: 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - needs a render test with a mocked useAudioView returning rvToast; not built this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioView/index.tsx:115 <div className={`absolute bottom-4 right-4 z-50 ...`}> (no role, no aria-live)
instrument: render AudioView with vi.mock(useAudioView) returning rvToast {message,type}; assert getByRole("status") holds the message (red today)

title: Deleting an audio event is one click with no undo
body:
## Summary
The Event Catalog row X deletes an event immediately with no confirmation or undo.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioEventCatalog/CategoryGroup.tsx:179-187 calls onDelete on click; AudioEventCatalog/index.tsx deleteEvent filters the row out and the write-through effect persists the loss to the per-scene store at once. The X is hover-revealed beside the row click target, so a mis-click loses a curated row (trigger, tags, bound sound set). Fixed = an undo toast (preferred for a cheap, frequent action) or the shared ConfirmDialog.

## Flow
- user hovers a row and clicks X (or tabs to it and presses Enter) -> deleteEvent -> setEvents -> useAudioEventCatalogStore.setEvents persists
- no way back short of re-entering the row

## Expected impact
Designers stop losing curated event rows to mis-clicks; measured by a test where delete then Undo restores the row. Risk: an extra step on intentional deletes.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an accidental delete is recoverable
Before: 0 of 1 deletes recoverable (read CategoryGroup.tsx:179-187, index.tsx deleteEvent)
After: 1 of 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - undo-vs-confirm is a UX choice the round did not settle
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: delete a row, click Undo, assert the row (same id, tags, assetSetId) is back in byScene[sceneId]

title: Legacy event catalog is inherited by every scene, not just the first
body:
## Summary
The store comment says the pre-scoping global catalog is attributed to whichever scene first opens the tab; the code hands it to every scene forever, including scenes created long after the migration.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/audioEventCatalogStore.ts:13-18 says legacy data "is attributed to whichever scene first opens the tab"; getEvents (audioEventCatalogStore.ts:50-56) returns `legacyEvents` for ANY scene without its own slot, and legacyEvents is never cleared. BudgetStressPanel.tsx:43-45 repeats the same fallback. So a brand-new scene opens with an old curated list instead of DEFAULT_EVENTS. Either the comment or the behaviour is wrong; which one is a product decision (carry curation to all scenes vs. migrate once).

## Flow
- user upgraded from the v0 global catalog -> legacyEvents set
- user creates a new scene today -> Event Catalog shows the legacy list, not defaults
- fix A: correct the comment; fix B: clear legacyEvents after first adoption

## Expected impact
Settles what a new scene starts with. Fix B changes what existing users see on new scenes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - store doc matches store behaviour
Before: 1 doc claim contradicted by code (comment vs getEvents)
After: 0
Method: simulation - walked getEvents for a second never-edited scene: returns legacyEvents
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/components/modules/content/audio/audioEventCatalogStore.ts:16-17 "it is attributed to whichever scene first opens the tab"
src/components/modules/content/audio/audioEventCatalogStore.ts:55 return get().legacyEvents;  (never nulled)

title: One read rule for a scene's event catalog, not three
body:
## Summary
The "own slot, else legacy, else defaults" rule for a scene's events is implemented three times.

## Description
audioEventCatalogStore.ts:50-56 (getEvents: own ?? legacy), AudioEventCatalog/index.tsx:240 (getEvents ?? structuredClone(DEFAULT_EVENTS)) and AudioView/BudgetStressPanel.tsx:43-45 (own ?? legacy ?? DEFAULT_EVENTS, via two selectors). The stress test must stress exactly the catalog the editor shows; a change to the legacy rule (see the legacy-inheritance card) applied in getEvents alone would make them disagree. Fixed = one exported selector `selectSceneEvents(state, sceneId)` used by all three.

## Flow
- change getEvents legacy handling -> Event Catalog changes -> BudgetStressPanel still reads legacy directly -> stress run diverges from the catalog

## Expected impact
Developers change the rule in one place; measured as implementations 3 -> 1 with a parity test. Risk: selector identity churn causing re-renders if it allocates.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the read rule
Before: 3 implementations (grep byScene/legacyEvents readers)
After: 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - not built: wants a parity test across editor and stress panel
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: parity test: for {own, legacy-only, empty} store states assert AudioEventCatalog initial rows === BudgetStressPanel rows

title: Validate event name and trigger before generating the audio manager
body:
## Summary
Generate Audio Manager accepts empty names, empty triggers and duplicate triggers, and cooldown has no ceiling.

## Description
AudioEventCatalog/index.tsx Generate is disabled only when `events.length === 0`. EventEditor name/trigger inputs accept "" and any string; two rows can share a trigger (OnCustomEvent is the default for every added row), and cooldown is clamped only at 0 (EventEditor.tsx:203 and the BudgetStressPanel cooldown input). buildAudioEventPrompt then asks the generator to bind the same gameplay hook twice or a blank one. The registry technique event-priority-concurrency-cooldown says Trigger is "a named gameplay hook". Fixed = inline row errors + Generate blocked with a named reason for empty/duplicate triggers; a cooldown ceiling.

## Flow
- user adds two Combat events without renaming -> both trigger OnCustomEvent -> Generate -> prompt lists the same trigger twice
- user clears a trigger -> Generate still enabled

## Expected impact
Generated managers stop carrying duplicate/blank bindings; measured as invalid rows reaching the prompt. Risk: blocking Generate on existing catalogs that already hold duplicates.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - only well-formed rows reach the generator
Before: 2 added rows -> 2 identical triggers in the prompt (walked addEvent defaults)
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - needs a component test over the onGenerate config
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: add two events, click Generate, assert onGenerate is not called (or config has no duplicate trigger) and a reason is shown

title: Clamp audio scene pool and voice limit on the server too
body:
## Summary
The UI now clamps Sound Pool Size / Max Concurrent Sounds to integers in range, but PUT /api/audio-scene stores whatever arrives.

## Description
src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts:110-111 maps soundPoolSize/maxConcurrentSounds straight to columns; src/lib/audio-codegen.ts:919-920 emits them as int32. A replayed request, another client path or an older client can still store 2.5 or 99999. Mirrors clampConfigInt in src/lib/economy/normalize-config.ts. Out of this context (audio-module / api).

## Flow
- PUT /api/audio-scene {soundPoolSize: 2.5} -> stored -> codegen int32 SoundPoolSize = 2.5;

## Expected impact
Codegen can never emit a fractional int32. Risk: none visible.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - server enforces the int range
Before: 0 of 2 fields clamped server-side
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - out-of-scope file
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/audio-scene-db.ts:110 { key: 'soundPoolSize', column: 'sound_pool_size' }
src/lib/audio-codegen.ts:919 int32 SoundPoolSize = ${doc.soundPoolSize};
instrument: db/route test: updateAudioScene({id, soundPoolSize: 2.5, maxConcurrentSounds: 999}) stores 2 / 128

title: Drop the two unused members useAudioView returns
body:
## Summary
useAudioView returns setActiveDocId and updateDoc; its only consumer never reads them.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioView/useAudioView.ts returns setActiveDocId and updateDoc; `grep -rn "useAudioView()" src` finds one consumer (AudioView/index.tsx:89) whose destructure names neither. Scene switching must go through sceneSession.requestSwitch (it waits for the open scene's write); exposing raw setActiveDocId invites a caller to bypass that guard.

## Flow
- remove both from the return object; typecheck proves no consumer

## Expected impact
Smaller hook surface; removes a bypass of the scene-switch save guard. Risk: test mocks still list them (harmless).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no dead exports
Before: 2 returned members with 0 consumers (grep)
After: 0
Method: probe - grep over src for consumers
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn "useAudioView()" src -> src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioView/index.tsx:89 only; its destructure omits setActiveDocId, updateDoc
instrument: whole-tree typecheck after removal (compare failing paths)
